claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled 'SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi' exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ and covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration to Pulumi.
In its early days SST was built on top of AWS CDK, which lets developers define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.
Ion is the code name for SST's new deployment engine that deploys components using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation; once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
AWS CDK is AWS-only, supports only TypeScript and Python, and is slower due to CloudFormation, while Pulumi supports any programming language and is faster.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` needs no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account, not Pulumi Cloud.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST apps define infrastructure in a single sst.config.ts file.
Through 2023, SST's provisioning layer was built directly on AWS CDK and CloudFormation.
In late 2023 the SST team began a rewrite code-named Ion that replaced the entire deployment layer.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST blog 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'

SST blog 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'When you run `sst deploy`, those resources make a call to an embedded Pulumi engine that makes a call to their bridged Terraform provider, and this makes the AWS SDK calls to create your resources.'
SST docs 'What is SST' say: 'SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.'
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: 'You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now.'
SST's platform package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds, and more, plus the Pulumiverse Vercel provider.
The SST repository is anomalyco/sst, formerly sst/sst.
The Pulumi engine diffs desired vs actual state, builds a dependency graph, and orders operations.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine doesn't require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API works by embedding Pulumi programs inside other tools.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric's docs state 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`; Defang deploys Docker Compose apps to the cloud.
Raw Pulumi resources can be defined inside an SST app alongside SST components and deployed in the same app.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The sst npm package gets roughly 796,000 downloads a week (796,291 for September 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode has a larger GitHub following than SST itself.
SST doesn't invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
Blog post aws-cdk-vs-pulumi-why-sst-switched exists at /blog/aws-cdk-vs-pulumi-why-sst-switched/.
